items.title: Weekly Pool Maintenance Checklist
items.summary: A simple, foolproof checklist for skimming, testing chemical balances, emptying skimmer baskets, and inspecting filter pressures to keep water crystal clear.
items.content:
Keeping your pool water pristine requires consistency. Follow this weekly checklist:
1. Skim surface debris daily or every other day to prevent organics from sinking and decaying.
2. Check and balance pH (7.4–7.6) and free chlorine (2.0–4.0 ppm).
3. Empty skimmer and pump strainer baskets to safeguard suction pressure.
4. Brush pool walls and tile lines to dislodge early stage algae and scale.
5. Backwash sand/DE filters or rinse cartridge elements when pressure rises 8-10 PSI above baseline.
6. Shock weekly or after heavy pool parties or rainstorms to oxidize contaminants.

items.title: Signs Your Pool Pump Needs Service
items.summary: Loud grinding noises, low water flow, leaking seals, or overheating are early warning signs your pump motor or impeller requires urgent servicing.
items.content:
Your pool pump is the heart of your circulation system. Watch for these 4 signs:
1. Screeching or Grinding Sounds: Worn motor bearings typically emit a high-pitched grinding sound that indicates the motor needs rebuild or replacement.
2. Low Water Flow & Priming Struggles: Air leaks in the suction line or clogged impellers reduce water turnover and leave air pockets in the pump basket.
3. Dripping Water Under Motor: Shaft seal failure allows chlorinated water into the motor housing, causing premature failure if not addressed quickly.
4. Circuit Breaker Tripping: Electrical shorting or excessive amp draw often indicates thermal overload or seizing windings.

items.title: Opening Your Pool After Wintertime
items.summary: Essential steps for removing winter covers, reconnecting pump and heater lines, initial chemical shock treatments, and establishing spring turnover.
items.content:
Start the swimming season with crystal clear results:
1. Clean and drain winter covers before removal to prevent contaminated puddle water from spilling into the pool.
2. Remove winterizing freeze plugs from return jets and skimmers, and reinstall drain plugs on pumps, filters, and heaters.
3. Bring water level back to mid-skimmer height and prime the filtration system.
4. Run circulation continuously for 24-48 hours while testing alkalinity, calcium hardness, stabilizer, and pH before chlorine shock.
5. Apply professional algaecide and clarifier to eliminate dormant winter spores.
